AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  FEBRUARY 7, 2023
  UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF
  ASSEMBLY BILL 361, WHICH ALLOWS COUNCIL MEMBERS TO PARTICIPATE FROM A REMOTE
LOCATION WITHOUT LISTING A PHYSICAL LOCATION. TO PROVIDE COMMENTS DURING A MEETING:
YOU MAY ATTEND THE MEETING, SEND AN EMAIL TO: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, OR JOIN THE
ZOOM MEETING BY CALLING: (669) 900-6833 OR USING THE ZOOM APP WITH THE FOLLOWING LINK:
  https://us02web.zoom.us/j/7095732685; MEETING ID: 709 573 2685. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED
 THROUGH ZOOM, FIOS CHANNEL 32 OR CHARTER CHANNEL 3, OR ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT:
  https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-agendas-393.
  6:00 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Ana Valencia, Mayor
  Margarita L. Rios, Vice Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Councilmember
  Jennifer Perez, Councilmember
  Rick Ramirez, Councilmember
 Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
 the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
 subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
 minutes.

 Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
 certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
 matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

 Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

 Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
 meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
 devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
 documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
 Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
 that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

 Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
 has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

 Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
 during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
 telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  CLOSED SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.
 CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Valencia

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Property: Front Street properties, Assessor Property Numbers 8056-015-014 and 8056-025-
  020; Negotiating Parties: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager, on behalf of the City and Arturo Sneider,
  Primestor Development Inc.; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment.

  II.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Property: a portion of the Metropolitan State Hospital, 11401 Bloomfield Avenue; Negotiating
  Parties: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager, on behalf of the City and Stephanie Clendenin, Director of
  State Hospitals; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment.

  III.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  54956.8 – Property: Norwalk Entertainment District, Assessor Parcel Nos. 8047-006-922, 8047-006-
  924, 8047-006-925; Negotiating Parties: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager, on behalf of the City and
  Arturo Sneider, Primestor Development Inc.; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment.

  IV.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – EXISTING LITIGATION PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT
  CODE §54956.9(d)(1), Norwalk v. City of Cerritos, Case No. LASC 22STCV33737.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Valencia

INVOCATION
  Pastor Danny Casas
  Remnant Church

FLAG SALUTE
  Abraham Alejandro Rivera, 7th grader
  Los Alisos Middle School

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

  I.  City Council to recognize the 2022 Angel Tree donors.

  II.  City Council to recognize the 2022 Stuff-A-Bus donors.

  III.  City Council to recognize the Santa Sleigh Foundation.
   IV.  City Council to proclaim February 6 - 10, 2023 as National School Counseling Week in the City of
  Norwalk.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  COVID-19 Update.

  2.  Supervisor Janice Hahn to present a check to the City for the Homeless Plan.

  3.  Chamber of Commerce 100th Anniversary.

  4.  Angel Tree Recap video.

  5.  Chick-fil-A Ribbon Cutting video.

  6.  Transit Village Project video.

  7.  Bi-Weekly Review.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meeting of January
  17, 2023. 825-04

  Minutes

  2.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period January 8, 2023 –
  January 21, 2023, in the total amount of $1,079,636.05. 630

  Report

  3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period
  January 10, 2023 through January 30, 2023 in the total amount of $5,422,996.13. 640

  Warrants

  4.  CLAIMS AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claims filed by Mercury
  Insurance on behalf of Brent Allen and Mercedes Valencia. 830-01/22

  Report

  5.  PLANNING COMMISSION SYNOPSIS – JANUARY 25, 2023 - No action is required. 320

  Report

  6.  RESOLUTION NO. 23-07 - DESTRUCTION OF OBSOLETE RECORDS FOR THE CITY CLERK’S
  DEPARTMENT – Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 23-07, A RESOLUTION OF
  THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK AUTHORIZING THE DESTRUCTION OF
  CERTAIN RECORDS IN THE CITY CLERK DEPARTMENT.

  Report

  7.  AGREEMENT - CONSULTING SERVICES FOR BUS STOP ASSESSMENT AND INVENTORY FOR
  NORWALK TRANSIT SYSTEM BUS STOP IMPROVEMENT PROJECT - Staff recommends City
  Council approve an agreement with Precision Material Management, LLC in an amount not to exceed
  $39,898 from March 1, 2023 through June 30, 2023; and authorize the City Manager to execute the
  agreement and any amendments provided there is funding in the budget and it is within the City
  Manager’s signing authority, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney.

  Report
   8.  APPROVAL OF NORWALK SENIOR CITIZENS CENTER, INC. BOARD OF DIRECTORS - Staff
  recommends City Council approve the nominations of the Norwalk Senior Citizens Center, Inc. Board
  of Directors for one-year terms to expire December 31, 2023.

  Report

  9.  RESOLUTION NO. 23-08 - APPLICATION FOR GRANT FUNDING FROM THE CALIFORNIA
  DEPARTMENT OF HOUSING AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT’S CALHOME PROGRAM - Staff
  recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 23-08, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF
  THE CITY OF NORWALK AUTHORIZING THE SUBMISSION OF AN APPLICATION TO THE
  CALIFORNIA STATE DEPARTMENT OF HOUSING AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT FOR
  FUNDING UNDER THE CALHOME PROGRAM; THE EXECUTION OF A STANDARD AGREEMENT
  IF SELECTED FOR SUCH FUNDING AND ANY AMENDMENTS THERETO; AND ANY RELATED
  DOCUMENTS NECESSARY TO PARTICIPATE IN THE CALHOME PROGRAM.

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  10. ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

REPORTS

  11. APPROVAL OF OPTION AGREEMENT FOR THE EXCHANGE OF REAL PROPERTY WITHIN THE
  HEART OF NORWALK PROJECT AREA - Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  find that the Option Agreement is exempt pursuant to California Environmental Quality Act
  Guidelines Section 15060(c)(3);

  b.  approve the Option Agreement with Primestor Development, LLC for City-owned Assessor Parcel
  Numbers 8056-015-900 and 8056-015-901 and grant the exclusive right to exchange for the
  property located at 13400 San Antonio Drive (Assessor Parcel Numbers 8056-015-014 and 8056-
  015-016); and

  c.  authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement, amendments and any documents in
  connection with the Option Agreement provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the
  City, in a form approved by the City Attorney.

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated February 2, 2023.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
